Consume a manifest, or refuse it loudly

Source: R/verify.R
consume_manifest.Rd

The consumer-side guard. Checks that the object is a manifest, that its schema version is one the caller declared it accepts, and that its payload still verifies, and errors informatively on any of the three rather than proceeding.

Usage

consume_manifest(m, accept = manifest_version())

Arguments

m

The manifest to consume.

accept

A character vector of accepted contract versions. Defaults to manifest_version(), the version this package implements. Widen it deliberately, per consumer, when a consumer has been shown to read an older schema correctly.

Value

m, invisibly, when all three checks pass. Errors otherwise.

Details

The version check is the point. Coercing silently across a schema boundary is how a pipeline ends up reading a slot that means something else than it did when the consumer was written, and the failure surfaces far downstream as a wrong number rather than an error. Declaring the accepted set makes the boundary explicit and moves the failure to the seam where it belongs.

See also

verify_manifest() for the non-erroring integrity check.

Author

Max Moldovan

Examples

params <- data.frame(a = c(0.1, 0.2))
m <- orchestra_manifest(
  emitter_package = "example",
  emitter_version = "0.1.0",
  inferential_target = "parameters",
  run_id = "example-001",
  method = "example:demo",
  seed = 1L,
  params = params,
  timestamp = Sys.time(),
  data_hash = manifest_data_hash(params, NULL, NULL, NULL, 1L)
)
identical(consume_manifest(m), m)
#> [1] TRUE

# A consumer that only reads a future schema refuses this one.
try(consume_manifest(m, accept = "9.9.9"))
#> Error : consume_manifest(): manifest_version '2.0.0-draft' is not in the accepted set {9.9.9} -- refusing to consume rather than silently coerce across a schema boundary
